product.disclosure: This video contains a promotional recommendation. The linked product is a paid digital product; check its current contents and terms on the sales page before buying.

productionRules: Target 6–10 minutes of original narration per long-form video; confirm final runtime against recorded audio.

Wildlife visuals must be genuine original creator-captured media only; retain creator identity, capture provenance, original source file and SHA-256, written commercial rights, third-party-rights review and human review for every asset.

Stock/library wildlife footage, Pexels/Pixabay wildlife footage and AI-generated wildlife visuals are prohibited production substitutes. Use clearly labelled diagrams or blank placeholders when qualifying original footage is unavailable.
Verify every wildlife fact against reliable sources before recording and distinguish observed behaviour from interpretation.

Keep promotional and non-commercial identities separate. The Nile crocodile documentary has hasPaidPromotion=false and no product CTA. Creator-education content uses the exact owner-approved direct-sales disclosure and approved product URL.
No automatic upload, scheduling or publication. Final render, rights, narration, captions, thumbnail, disclosures and exact-hash human approval are separate gates.

episodes.workingTitle: Two Eyes Above the Water: The Hidden Hunting System of the Nile Crocodile
episodes.audience: Wildlife documentary viewers interested in African freshwater predators
episodes.viewerPromise: Explain how the Nile crocodile's waterline posture, sensory systems and ambush behaviour work together, without exaggerating research or depicting fabricated encounters.
episodes.hook: At first, the river seems empty. Then, just above the waterline, two eyes appear.

beats: Introduce the low-profile posture
Set the documentary's central question
Explain eyes, nostrils and ears near the waterline
Avoid describing concealment as magic
Explain integumentary sensory organs
Distinguish experimental findings from claims about every wild hunt
Explain opportunity and surprise
Avoid implying all crocodiles behave identically
Place crocodiles in freshwater ecosystems
Give conservative public-safety guidance

episodes.viewerPromise: A repeatable planning process for building a clear story before editing.
episodes.hook: A collection of beautiful animal clips is not automatically a compelling video. The difference is usually the story connecting them.

beats: Show a contrast between disconnected clips and a story-led sequence
Promise a practical planning method
Define one central question
Avoid trying to cover an entire species in one video

outline.section: Build a beginning, middle and payoff
beats: Set up the situation
Introduce a challenge or change
Resolve the question without inventing animal behavior
List facts that need verification
Separate observed footage from narration and inference
Match each scene to a narration beat
Use only rights-cleared visuals and sound
Avoid repetitive shots and misleading edits
Make the promise specific and accurate
Check captions, sources, rights and disclosures
Invite viewers to explore the approved creator resource
State that it is a paid product and results are not guaranteed

episodes.workingTitle: A Beginner Workflow for Faceless Wildlife Videos
episodes.audience: Creators building a faceless wildlife or nature channel on a small budget
episodes.viewerPromise: A practical, rights-aware production workflow from research to final review.
episodes.hook: You can work without appearing on camera, but a faceless format still needs original value, careful research and visuals you have permission to use.

beats: Explain the faceless format
Set realistic expectations: no guaranteed growth or monetization
Write a single audience question
Use reliable sources and record citations
Use a clear hook, context, progression and payoff
Distinguish verified facts from uncertainty
Prefer self-created or explicitly licensed assets
Track creator, source, license and usage conditions
Never assume a search result is free to reuse
Match scenes to narration
Use readable captions and clean audio
Avoid fabricated scenes or deceptive animal interactions
Align title and thumbnail with the actual video
Check factual accuracy, caption timing and disclosure
Review YouTube policies before upload
Mention the approved paid creator resource without pressure
No claims of guaranteed results

metadata.title: A Beginner Workflow for Faceless Wildlife Videos
metadata.description: Unassigned creator-education draft. This workflow covers focused research, narration, genuine original creator-captured wildlife visuals, editing, captions and final review. It is not assigned a publication-cycle position and is not production-approved.

limitations: These briefs are not completed scripts, narration files, rendered MP4s or scheduled uploads.
The existing long-form renderer still requires real footage, narration, captions, rights evidence and human approval.
The verified YouTube channel ID is still required before private upload can be enabled.
